strengths: UniAP addresses a useful problem for large vision models: automatically selecting pipeline placement together with DP, TP, and FSDP strategies. Combining hardware profiling, memory constraints, and joint strategy selection is a worthwhile systems contribution.

Table 1 demonstrates meaningful throughput gains. On ENVB-8, UniAP achieves 45.58 samples/s for ViT-Huge versus Alpa’s 38.74, and 19.08 for Swin-Huge versus Galvatron’s 13.90. The reported 3.80× improvement for Llama-7B is substantial. Matching Galvatron’s throughput with shorter search times on several ENVA workloads also provides practical value.

The evaluation covers five model families and four hardware environments, including non-NVIDIA accelerators. The experiments extend to 64 devices under weak scaling, and UniAP matches the best measured Megatron candidates on the DCU experiments while substantially reducing strategy-search time.

The overall workflow and BERT case study are understandable. Appendix D provides useful model and solver configurations, while Appendix E reports a promising average throughput-estimation error of 3.59% on the selected configurations.
weaknesses: The decisive concern is a correctness gap in the stage-placement formulation. Equations (6a–6c) enforce contiguity, but not increasing pipeline-stage order along graph edges. For a two-layer chain u→v, placing u on stage 2 and v on stage 1 satisfies these constraints and the placement constraints. Equation (4) then assigns zero communication cost to their edge because it counts only transfers from stage j to j+1. Thus the written optimization can favor assignments with incorrectly omitted communication. Appendix A proves contiguity but does not resolve this issue.

The claimed MIQP is incompletely specified. Equations (3) and (4) contain degree-four products involving two placement variables and two strategy-selection variables. The auxiliary variables and constraints needed to obtain a quadratic or linear mixed-integer formulation are absent. This is a correctable specification gap, but it leaves the actual solver model and its computational size unclear.

The repeated claim of finding an optimal solution is not established by the reported solver procedure. Appendix D specifies a 60-second limit and permits termination after 15 seconds with an optimality gap below 4%; achieved gaps and timeout frequencies are not reported. Moreover, solver optimality would apply to the estimated cost within the enumerated strategy space. Section 3.5’s polynomial runtime argument follows from capping solver time and does not establish the complexity of obtaining an exact optimum.

The memory model does not adequately explain GPipe activation retention. Algorithm 1 constructs the memory costs using micro-batch size b=B/c, while Equation (5) has no explicit dependence on the number of retained micro-batches. Under the stated GPipe schedule with checkpointing disabled, activations from multiple micro-batches remain live. The manuscript needs to establish how this storage enters M; successful selected runs alone do not validate the claimed memory-feasibility guarantee.

The evidence does not isolate the central claim that joint optimization explains the advantage over hierarchical methods. Figure 6 compares the full method with inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants, rather than a hierarchical variant using the same cost model and candidate strategies. Appendix E also reports substantially different cost-model accuracy between UniAP and Galvatron. These results support combining parallelism categories, but do not determine how much benefit comes specifically from joint search. Hierarchical optimization alone does not imply suboptimality.

The practical search-time advantage is incompletely characterized. The timing metric covers UOP and excludes profiling, and Section 4.2 attributes substantial speedups to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baselines without reporting comparable CPU resource budgets. The measured search times are useful, but total planning overhead and the contribution of resource allocation remain uncertain.
